takeaways: People can postpone or turn off interruptions, such as pop-ups, alerts and automatic updates, except interruptions about an emergency.
It is Level AAA. 2.2.2 covers moving and auto-updating content, and 4.1.3 covers whether status messages are announced. 2.2.4 is about letting people choose when interruptions reach them.
Interruptions break concentration and can move a screen reader or magnifier away from where someone is working. Getting back costs real time.
Designers own most of this: which messages interrupt at all, how they can be snoozed or muted, and where they wait until people are ready.
failures: A newsletter pop-up that appears mid-article with no way to stop it
A news feed that refreshes and jumps while people read
Chat messages that pop over the form people are filling in, with no mute
check: List everything that can appear without the person asking: pop-ups, chat, notifications, alerts, refreshes.
For each, find the control to postpone or turn it off, such as snooze, Do not disturb or a notification setting.
Mark which items are true emergencies, such as safety alerts, and keep that list short.

quiz.question: A dashboard shows a pop-up every time a new comment arrives. Which design meets 2.2.4?
options: Add a Do not disturb setting, and collect comments in an inbox people can open when ready
Make the pop-up smaller and move it to the corner
Close the pop-up automatically after 5 seconds
quiz.why: A smaller or self-closing pop-up still interrupts, and a timed close can take away the message before people read it. Letting people mute or delay comments, and find them later, puts them in control.

spec: List each interruption, what triggers it, and whether it can be postponed or turned off.
Design the controls: snooze, Do not disturb, notification settings, and where held messages wait.
Name any emergency messages that cannot be suppressed, and why.
review: Who asked for this to interrupt, and could it wait?
Where can people turn this off, and will they find it?
Is this really an emergency, or just important to us?
tradeoff: Growth and support teams want messages to be seen right away. Hold non-urgent messages in a place people will check, and keep the right to interrupt for real emergencies only.
system: Give the notification component a priority level and a user setting, so only emergency alerts bypass Do not disturb.
pitch: Every pop-up costs someone their place. Letting people choose when to see updates keeps them working, and keeps them coming back.
